national_raw_news.content: Praising the remarkable achievement of India’s rise in fintech, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that the country’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) is the undisputed champion of this success story. Inaugurating the ‘Global Fintech Fest 2026’ in Mumbai, Mr Modi said this is such a massive transformation that whenever fintech is discussed, it will remain incomplete without UPI. Reiterating his core philosophy of technological empowerment, the Prime Minister praised UPI as the ultimate tool for financial inclusion, successfully penetrating areas ignored by traditional banking models. The Prime Minister pointed out that over 24 billion UPI transactions occurred in August alone. Mr Modi said that because of this impact, French President Emmanuel Macron said that UPI is not just a tech story; it is a civilizational story. Highlighting the global expansion of India’s flagship digital payment system, Prime Minister said that UPI is now live in 11 countries, turning what was once unimaginable into an everyday reality for international payments. Outlining the next strategic phase for international digital payments, Mr Modi emphasised the urgent need to integrate UPI with the domestic payment systems of partner countries, mirroring the seamless cross-border connectivity already established with Singapore. He directed stakeholders to actively link financial networks wherever large Indian populations reside or extensive trade occurs. Emphasising the economic benefits for the diaspora, PM Modi pointed out that reducing transaction costs for the world’s largest remittance-sending population is a critical priority. He explained that integrating digital payment systems globally would significantly accelerate the transfer of funds to families back home.

national_raw_news.title: 6 hours ago | National 202 Defence Minister Rajnath Singh describes Indian community in Sri Lanka as important bridge betwee...
national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has described Indian community in Sri Lanka as a bridge between the two countries, saying they play a crucial role in strengthening friendship between the two nations. Mr Singh, who reached Colombo yesterday on a three-day visit to Sri Lanka, made the remarks while interacting with members of the Indian diaspora. The Defence Minister said that India will always stand firmly with Sri Lanka in times of crisis, underlining that the relationship between the two countries is based on shared history, culture and faith. He said both nations share close cultural and civilisational ties, which have provided a strong foundation for the growth of the bilateral relationship. In his address, Mr Singh highlighted India’s rapid economic transformation, saying the country is among the fastest-growing major economies in the world and contributes more than 16 per cent to global growth. Noting that India’s economy grew at 7.8 per cent in the first quarter of 2026-27 amid global economic challenges, Mr. Singh pointed out that India has concluded trade deals with 38 countries over the last 12 years, including Free Trade Agreements (FTA) with eight major nations. Referring to the India-European Union FTA as the ‘Mother of All Deals’, he said the agreement opens access to the massive EU market and reflects India’s growing diplomatic and economic capabilities. Mr. Singh credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi for the significant rise in India’s global credibility, saying that compared to 12 years ago, the world today listens when India speaks on the international stage. Mr Singh, who is leading a high-level delegation comprising senior officials from the ministries of defence and external affairs, was received at the Bandaranaike International Airport by Sri Lanka’s Deputy Minister of Defence Maj Gen (Retd) Aruna Jayasekara.

national_raw_news.title: 6 hours ago | International 117 Canada Hits More Than 600 US Products with Tariffs Up to 50%
national_raw_news.content: Canada has imposed retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on more than 600 US goods, escalating the trade dispute between two neighbours. The tariffs targeting US merchandise officially came into force last night. Canadian commercial enterprises are operating under the federal government’s newly implemented dollar-for-dollar tariffs, covering approximately 28 billion US dollars’ worth of American imports. The measures, which took effect at midnight, impose tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on more than 600 US products. The affected goods include industrial materials such as steel and aluminium, household essentials such as toilet paper, and specialised products such as coin-operated arcade machines. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump has ordered federal agencies to stop purchasing Canadian products through the government’s primary procurement catalogue until Ottawa provides American businesses and farmers with equal access to the Canadian market. The directive instructs the General Services Administration (GSA) and the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) to immediately begin removing Canadian products from federal procurement channels. In a social media post, Trump accused Canada of unfair trade practices, alleging that Canadian federal and provincial governments prevent American small businesses from selling to public-sector entities while Canadian companies enjoy relatively open access to US government contracts.

national_raw_news.title: Indian Contingent for Asian Games 2026 Receives Grand Send-off in New Delhi 8 hours ago 128
national_raw_news.content: The Indian contingent for the Asian Games 2026 received a grand send-off in New Delhi yesterday in the presence of Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya. Dr. Mandaviya, along with Indian Olympic Association President P T Usha, Sports Secretary Hari Ranjan Rao, and Chef de Mission Sahdev Yadav, unveiled the official jersey of the Indian contingent in the presence of athletes and support staff. Addressing the gathering, Dr. Mandaviya urged Indian athletes to turn pressure into performance, view opponents as opportunities and transform those opportunities into achievements. Highlighting Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision for Indian sports, he said the Government has created new pathways for athletes to compete and excel at the global level. Dr Mandaviya also highlighted the growing depth of Indian sport and the emergence of young talent. He said that out of the 503-member contingent, more than three hundred athletes are first-time participants at the Asian Games. Applauding India’s performance at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow, the Union Minister said at the last Commonwealth Games, India won 13 gold medals and this time the tally has improved by more than 35 per cent. He said the target is to establish India firmly on the world sporting stage by 2036, when the country aims to host the Olympic Games. He added that this ten-year plan includes an allocation of more than 36 thousand crore rupees for improving sports infrastructure. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports informed us that the Asian Games 2026 will be held in Japan, where the Indian contingent will compete across multiple sporting disciplines. The 503-member contingent includes athletes and support staff, with more than three hundred athletes set to make their debut at the Asian Games, reflecting the growing depth and bench strength of Indian sport.

national_raw_news.title: 9th National Nutrition Month Inaugurated in Varanasi by CM Yogi Adityanath and Union Minister Annapurna Devi 12 mins ago 5
national_raw_news.content: The 9th National Nutrition Month was inaugurated with great fanfare at the International Rudraksh Convention Center in Varanasi today. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, along with Union Minister for Women and Child Development Annapurna Devi, inaugurated the program by lighting a lamp in the presence of Minister of State for Women and Child Development Savitri Thakur and other ministers of the Uttar Pradesh government. Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister Annapurna Devi said that through the 9th National Nutrition Month, it’s a commitment to a well-nourished and empowered India. This campaign is linked to the health of every mother, the nutrition of every child, and the prosperity of every family. She said that pure and balanced nutrition is a strong foundation for a healthy and prosperous nation. On this occasion, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, nutrition for the poor, children, pregnant women, and lactating mothers has been prioritised since 2014. The Anganwadi centre system in Uttar Pradesh has also undergone significant changes. These centres are now becoming centres not just for nutrition distribution but for children’s health, nutrition, and early development. He said that the spirit of “Our Anganwadi, Our Responsibility” must be transformed into a campaign of public participation. The inaugural event in Varanasi featured a nutrition fair, a video presentation based on beneficiaries’ experiences, and a dialogue between the Union Minister and Anganwadi workers. Additionally, the Chief Minister gathered feedback from Anganwadi workers from across the country on their work and sought suggestions on how to improve it. He along with Union Minister also inspected the stalls set up for the occasion.

national_raw_news.title: Mizoram’s Saitual Becomes First District in State to Achieve ‘Surakshit’ HIV Status 2 hours ago 41
national_raw_news.content: North-eastern Mizoram’s Saitual, bordering Manipur, has become the only district in Mizoram to attain ‘Surakshit’ status under the National AIDS Control Organisation (NACO)’s Mobilisation AIDS Suraksha (MAS) campaign after achieving all three of the 95-95-95 HIV treatment and prevention targets. Under the UNAIDS-linked 95-95-95 targets, 95% of all people estimated to be living with HIV should know their status, 95% of those diagnosed should receive antiretroviral therapy (ART), and 95% of those on treatment should achieve viral load suppression. Districts under the MAS campaign are classified into four categories based on their performance: Sangharshee for those yet to achieve any of the three targets, Saksham for those meeting two, Surakshit for those achieving all three, and Surakshit+ for districts that also achieve zero mother-to-child transmission of HIV. The MAS campaign, launched in February, aims to break the chain of HIV transmission by achieving the 95-95-95 goals across the country. District-level progress is reviewed regularly under the leadership of deputy commissioners. According to the August report, Saitual achieved Surakshit status, becoming the first and only district in Mizoram to reach the milestone. Deputy Chief Medical Officer Dr Zothanpari Chhakchhuak credited the achievement to the support of Saitual Deputy Commissioner Srinivas Sadi and close cooperation from community leaders, NGOs and churches, particularly in promoting HIV testing and awareness campaigns. She stressed the need for continued large-scale testing to ensure people know their HIV status and urged those living with HIV to remain on ART regularly to sustain the district’s progress.
